join_order.notes: Russian companies are few hundred; CSR walk yields candidate movie rows directly
Filter movies by production_year > 2010 via direct column deref
For each movie, iterate ci rows in [lo,hi); ci is sorted by movie_id

join_order.build: ci rows passing role_id=actor AND note contains '(producer)'
join_order.notes: Direct deref into dense-PK char_name; update MIN aggregates

data_structures.candidate_movies: vector<uint8_t> bitset over title rows (2,528,312 bits)
data_structures.filtered_movies: implicit (iterate bitset and apply year filter inline)
data_structures.ci_indexes: use cast_info__movie_id offsets_only index for movie-id range scan
data_structures.aggregation: two scalar MIN holders: std::string min_chn_name, std::string min_title

parallelism.morsel_unit: ru_company_ids partitioned across threads; per-thread local MINs reduced at end
parallelism.notes: Only ~400 companies but each expands to thousands of mc rows; parallelize the outer driver loop

notes: Resolve rt_id_actor and ru_code via dict scans at startup.
Driver loop: for cid in ru_company_ids -> walk mc CSR -> set bit in movie bitset.
Second pass: for each set bit mv, check production_year[mv-1] > 2010, then walk ci offsets [lo,hi).
Per ci row r: check role_id[r] == rt_id_actor; if so, memmem note[off[r]..off[r+1]] for '(producer)'; if hit, deref person_role_id[r]; update MINs.
Per-thread local MIN strings to avoid contention; merge sequentially after parallel region.

Loads required columns: cn.country_code, mc.movie_id, mc.company_id (via CSR), title.production_year, title.title (off+dat), ci.role_id, ci.note (off+dat), ci.person_role_id, char_name.name (off+dat).

Skip company_type entirely: ct has no predicate and ct.id is dense-PK so the join with mc.company_type_id is structurally satisfied (mc rows always have valid ct id); no need to load company_type files.
